title: addons
text:
WorkspaceAddons manages HTTP add-on deployments and per-user test installation without depending on Google’s discovery endpoint. It uses fastgws’ authenticated, refreshing, retrying transport against the documented REST paths; the discovery-backed GWSApi remains the default for services whose discovery document is available.
source

WorkspaceAddons
def WorkspaceAddons(
    project:str, # Google Cloud project ID or number
    creds, # Google OAuth credentials with `scope`
    timeout:float=60, # Request timeout in seconds
):
Workspace Add-ons deployment and test-installation client

title: addons
text:
Project and deployments
Authorization exposes the service-account identity Google uses for system ID tokens and the OAuth client audience used for user ID tokens. Deployment listing is a read-only way to inspect the project before changing it.


source

WorkspaceAddons.list_deployments
async def list_deployments():
List the project’s deployments




source

WorkspaceAddons.authorization
async def authorization():
Get the project’s add-on callback authorization identities


deploy uses the API’s replace operation: the same call creates a missing deployment or replaces an existing one. This gives iterative tooling one idempotent operation instead of a list-then-create-or-update branch.


source

WorkspaceAddons.deploy
async def deploy(
    deployment_id:str, # Stable deployment ID
    manifest:dict, # Deployment resource, without requiring its `name`
):
Create or replace a deployment

title: addons
text:
Test installation
Test installation belongs to the authenticated user, so use a separate WorkspaceAddons instance for each tester’s credentials. ensure_installed is the idempotent initial setup operation. After replacing a live development deployment, reinstall deliberately uninstalls and installs it again so host applications pick up the new callback configuration.


source

WorkspaceAddons.reinstall
async def reinstall(
    deployment_id:str
):
Reinstall a deployment and return its current status




source

WorkspaceAddons.ensure_installed
async def ensure_installed(
    deployment_id:str
):
Install a deployment when needed and return its current status




source

WorkspaceAddons.uninstall
async def uninstall(
    deployment_id:str
):
Uninstall a test deployment from this user




source

WorkspaceAddons.install
async def install(
    deployment_id:str
):
Install a deployment for this user to test




source

WorkspaceAddons.install_status
async def install_status(
    deployment_id:str
):
Get this user’s test-installation status


A complete first-time setup reads the callback identities, replaces one stable deployment, and ensures the active tester has it installed. Subsequent callback changes use reinstall after deploy:

creds = await oauth_creds(account='developer@example.com', internal=True,
    scopes=[WorkspaceAddons.scope])
addons = WorkspaceAddons('my-project', creds)
auth = await addons.authorization()
deployment = await addons.deploy('dev', manifest)
status = await addons.ensure_installed('dev')

updated = await addons.deploy('dev', updated_manifest)
refreshed = await addons.reinstall('dev')
(auth.serviceAccountEmail, updated.name, refreshed.installed)

title: fastgws
text: fastgws builds async Python clients for Google APIs from Google’s discovery documents. Each service gets a small Python surface: resource groups become attributes, operations become awaitable methods, and responses come back as lightweight objects instead of raw JSON dictionaries.

title: fastgws
text:
Installation
Install from pypi:
$ pip install fastgws
Or install the latest development version from GitHub:
$ pip install git+https://github.com/answerdotai/fastgws.git

title: fastgws
text:
How to use
Import the service clients you want to use. Each client is built from Google’s discovery documents and exposes resource groups as Python attributes, so calls look like await drive.files.list(...) or await calendar.events.list(...).

from fastgws import Calendar, Docs, Drive, GMail, Places
from fastgws.auth import *

fastgws supports OAuth credentials and API keys. OAuth is the usual choice for Google Workspace APIs such as Gmail, Calendar, Drive, and Docs, because these APIs act on behalf of a user and require explicit scopes.
Credentials are gclientid’s job. It creates your Google Cloud project, consent configuration, and OAuth clients, stores one token per account and client, and loads, refreshes, and re-authorizes those tokens. fastgws depends on it and re-exports its token functions, so oauth_creds here is gclientid’s oauth_creds. This page shows how fastgws uses the credentials; read the gclientid README for provisioning, presets, the stored files, and re-authorization.
API keys are useful for public Google APIs that support key-based access, such as Places. You can pass api_key=... directly or set GOOGLE_API_KEY or GWS_API_KEY in the environment.

Use a gclientid token
Set up once with gclientid (see “Quick start” in the gclientid README), then authorize an account, choosing a preset or explicit scopes (“Access presets” there):
gclientid-auth me@example.com --preset google-apps
Then pass the account name instead of constructing a path:
creds = await oauth_creds(account='me@example.com')
The token records its granted scopes, so scopes is optional; when supplied, oauth_creds verifies that the token covers them. Access tokens are refreshed back into the same file during API calls, including after a 401. When a token is missing, lacks the scopes, or can no longer be refreshed, what happens is a gclientid setting: by default on a machine where gclientid ran, it re-authorizes in your browser and returns; otherwise it raises an error naming the gclientid-auth command to run (“Automatic re-authorization” in the gclientid README). Pass token_path= instead for an authorized-user file stored elsewhere.
internal=True and desktop=True select the tokens of gclientid’s Internal-audience and Desktop clients (“Stored files” in the gclientid README):
creds = await oauth_creds(account="me@example.com", internal=True)
creds = await oauth_creds(account="me@example.com", desktop=True)

scopes = ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar', 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents',
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly', 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly']
creds = await oauth_creds(account='me@example.com', scopes=scopes)

Auth complete


Responses are converted into lightweight Python objects. Known Google resource kinds get more specific classes such as FileList, Events, or Event; when a service does not provide enough schema information, fastgws falls back to the base GWSObject. Either way, fields are available as attributes as well as dictionary keys.
Use Docs to create a document, apply batch updates, and read the document back. The API accepts the same request dictionaries documented by Google, while fastgws handles auth, transport, and object conversion.

docs = Docs(creds=creds)
doc = await docs.documents.create(title='fastgws test doc')
doc


GWSObject(title='fastgws test doc', documentId='1ObmgD5GOA9zNZbUwCYeFZH8nUc_MKcJHKFqjPJGnkQs', body=1, documentStyle=11, namedStyles=1, tabs=1)




await docs.documents.batch_update(document_id=doc.documentId,
    requests=[{'insertText': {'location': {'index': 1},
        'text': 'Hello from fastgws\n'}}])


GWSObject(documentId='1ObmgD5GOA9zNZbUwCYeFZH8nUc_MKcJHKFqjPJGnkQs', replies=1, writeControl=1)




def doc_text(doc):
    return ''.join(e.textRun.content for b in doc.body.content if 'paragraph' in b for e in b.paragraph.elements if 'textRun' in e)

doc = await docs.documents.get(document_id=doc.documentId)
txt = doc_text(doc)
print(txt)

Hello from fastgws




Use Drive to search files and inspect metadata. This example returns a FileList, and its files collection contains file objects with attributes such as id, name, and mimeType.

drive = Drive(creds=creds)
fs = await drive.files.list(q="name contains 'fastgws' and trashed=false", page_size=10)
fs, fs.files[0]

(FileList(kind='drive#fileList', files=3),
 File(id='1ObmgD5GOA9zNZbUwCYeFZH8nUc_MKcJHKFqjPJGnkQs', name='fastgws test doc', mimeType='application/vnd.google-apps.document', kind='drive#file'))


Use Gmail to search messages with the Gmail query syntax. The result is still a Python object, so you can inspect message ids, thread ids, and any fields returned by the API without digging through raw JSON first.

gmail = GMail(creds=creds)
msgs = await gmail.users.messages.list(user_id='me', max_results=10)
msgs


GWSObject(messages=10)



List operations expose pages. The iterator forwards each nextPageToken as page_token and stops after the final page.
Every operation also exposes batch when its Google discovery document advertises a batch endpoint. Pass dictionaries containing the same arguments accepted by the operation; results preserve call order. fastgws uses Google’s recommended 50-call chunks by default (the protocol maximum is 100), and return_exceptions=True returns a structured APIError in the corresponding position instead of raising it.
messages = await gmail.users.messages.get.batch([
    dict(user_id='me', id=mid, format='minimal', fields='id,labelIds')
    for mid in message_ids
])
Ordinary and batched operations retry transient network failures, 429s, 5xx responses, and Google’s retryable 403 rate-limit reasons. Delays use Retry-After, then RetryInfo, then the reported quota window, then exponential backoff with jitter. max_wait limits each wait to 300 seconds by default. A longer required delay stops retries and preserves the original error. batch accepts these retry options for both the outer HTTP request and its failed parts. Ordinary transport calls accept them through GWSTransport.request.
A batch retries only its failed parts. Credentials refresh automatically after a 401. Credential refresh does not skip rate-limit waits. Clients request gzip responses by default. Use Google’s global fields argument, as above, to request a partial response when the complete resource is unnecessary.

pages = gmail.users.messages.list.pages(user_id='me', max_results=10)
first_page = await anext(pages)
first_page

Use Calendar to create, update, delete, and search events.

calendar = Calendar(creds=creds)
event = await calendar.events.insert(calendar_id='primary', summary='fastgws test event', start={'dateTime': '2030-01-01T09:00:00Z'},
    end={'dateTime': '2030-01-01T09:30:00Z'})
event


Event(id='u99k6q861u35h6mrmejdrgc0gg', summary='fastgws test event', kind='calendar#event', creator=2, organizer=2, start=2, end=2, reminders=1)




events = await calendar.events.list(calendar_id='primary', q='fastgws test event',
    max_results=10, single_events=True, order_by='startTime')
events, events['items'][0]

(Events(summary='nc@answer.ai', kind='calendar#events', defaultReminders=1, items=1),
 Event(id='u99k6q861u35h6mrmejdrgc0gg', summary='fastgws test event', kind='calendar#event', creator=2, organizer=2, start=2, end=2, reminders=1))



await calendar.events.delete(calendar_id='primary', event_id=event.id)

''


Use API-key services the same way. Places can run with an API key instead of OAuth credentials, and this example asks Google to return only the fields needed to render a link.

from IPython.display import Markdown


places = Places()
res = await places.places.search_text(text_query='coffee near San Francisco',
    _headers={'X-Goog-FieldMask':'places.displayName,places.formattedAddress,places.location,places.googleMapsUri'})
p = res.places[0]
Markdown(f'[{p.displayName.text}]({p.googleMapsUri})')


787 Coffee



fastgws can also create service clients dynamically from Google’s discovery index. If Google publishes a discovery document for a service, you can usually import that service by name, for example from fastgws import Sheets, then use it with the same creds, token, or api_key arguments shown above.
Services outside the central discovery index can be loaded from their own discovery URL. The discovery request uses the same credentials, token, API key, quota project, and custom headers as the resulting client.
drive = await GWSApi.from_discovery_url(
    'https://www.googleapis.com/discovery/v1/apis/drive/v3/rest',
    creds=creds)

title: fastgws
text:
Workspace Add-ons
WorkspaceAddons manages HTTP add-on deployments through the documented REST endpoints. It does not fetch the Workspace Add-ons discovery document. deploy creates or replaces one stable deployment ID, and ensure_installed installs it for the credentials’ user only when needed. After replacing a development deployment’s callback configuration, use reinstall so host applications pick up the change.
from fastgws import WorkspaceAddons

addons = WorkspaceAddons('my-project', creds)
auth = await addons.authorization()
deployment = await addons.deploy('dev', manifest)
status = await addons.ensure_installed('dev')
Create one client per tester because test installation belongs to the authenticated user.

title: fastgws
text:
Workspace administration
WorkspaceAdmin provides explicit user lifecycle operations over the Admin Directory and Enterprise License Manager APIs. Creation does not imply licensing: domains can auto-assign licences by organizational unit, or callers can use assign_license with the domain’s product SKU.
from fastgws import WorkspaceAdmin

admin = WorkspaceAdmin(creds)
user = await admin.create_user('new@example.com', 'New', 'User', password,
                               org_unit_path='/Internal')
await admin.assign_license(user.primaryEmail, 'workspace-sku-id')
Suspension, restoration, licence removal, and deletion are separate calls, so automated setup does not hide destructive lifecycle changes.

title: fastgws
text:
PySkill support
fastgws includes a PySkill for agents working inside solveit. Load fastgws.skill when a task needs access to Google Workspace or Google APIs through the base GWSApi client.
The skill exposes GWSApi, GWSObject, oauth_creds, and svc_acct_creds, and allows generated Google API operations through GWSOpFunc. Agents load an account’s existing gclientid token; authorization remains an explicit user action through gclientid-auth.
creds = await oauth_creds(account='me@example.com', scopes=['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly'])
gmail = GWSApi('gmail', creds=creds)
msgs = await gmail.users.messages.list(user_id='me', max_results=10)

GWSObject
def GWSObject(
    *args, **kwargs
):
dict subclass that also provides access to keys as attrs, and has a pretty markdown repr
GWSObject recursively wraps Google API responses while retaining concise representations for common resource fields.
files = g2obj({'files':[dict(id='report', name='Quarterly report', owners=[{'displayName':'Alex'}])]}, {})
test_eq(files.files[0].owners[0].displayName, 'Alex')
files.files[0], files.files[0].owners[0].displayName

title: core
text:
Retry handling
Google returns legacy reasons in error.errors and structured reasons in ErrorInfo entries in error.details. These reasons identify retryable 403 rate-limit errors. Other failures retain the transport’s retry classification.

rate_limited = APIError('Quota exceeded', status_code=403, raw={'error':{'errors':[{'reason':'userRateLimitExceeded'}]}})
forbidden = APIError('Permission denied', status_code=403)
test_eq((_retryable(rate_limited), _retryable(forbidden)), (True, False))
_retryable(rate_limited), _retryable(forbidden)

(True, False)


Retry-After accepts a number of seconds or an HTTP date. This date is 12 seconds after the supplied current time. Invalid values do not supply a delay.

dated_response = httpx2.Response(503, headers={'Retry-After':'Tue, 14 Nov 2023 22:13:32 GMT'})
dated_error = APIError('Service unavailable', status_code=503, response=dated_response)
test_eq(_retry_after(dated_error, now=1700000000), 12)
_retry_after(dated_error, now=1700000000)

12.0


RetryInfo.retryDelay is a duration in seconds, including fractional seconds.

retry_info = APIError('Try again later', status_code=429, raw={'error':{'details':[{
    '@type':'type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.RetryInfo', 'retryDelay':'2.5s'}]}})
test_eq(_retry_info(retry_info), 2.5)
_retry_info(retry_info)

2.5


A quota error can name its accounting window in ErrorInfo.metadata. Here the minute started 30 seconds ago. The retry waits for the remaining 30 seconds plus a one-second margin.

quota = APIError('Quota exceeded', status_code=403, raw={'error':{'details':[{
    '@type':'type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo', 'reason':'RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED',
    'metadata':{'quota_unit':'1/min/{project}/{user}', 'window_start_time':'1700000000'}}]}})
test_eq(_quota_wait(quota, now=1700000030), 31)
_quota_wait(quota, now=1700000030)

31.0


Retry delays use Retry-After, then RetryInfo.retryDelay, then quota-window metadata. If none supplies a valid delay, retries use exponential backoff with jitter. max_wait defaults to 300 seconds and applies to every delay source. Longer delays stop retries without shortening the required wait.

wait = _retry_delay(quota, 0, 1, 64, now=1700000030)
test_eq(wait, 31)
test_is(_retry_delay(quota, 0, 1, 64, max_wait=30, now=1700000030), None)
wait

31.0


Without a timing hint, a retryable error uses exponential backoff. A permission error without a rate-limit reason is not retryable.

unavailable = APIError('Service unavailable', status_code=503)
test_eq((_retryable(unavailable), _retryable(forbidden)), (True, False))
backoff = _retry_delay(unavailable, 2, 1, 64)
assert 4 <= backoff <= 5
backoff

4.694767496006301


An explicit Retry-After takes precedence over backoff. A wait limit rejects a longer delay instead of retrying early.

retry_response = httpx2.Response(503, headers={'Retry-After':'12'})
retry_error = APIError('Service unavailable', status_code=503, response=retry_response)
test_eq(_retry_delay(retry_error, 0, 1, 64), 12)
test_is(_retry_delay(retry_error, 0, 1, 64, max_wait=10), None)
_retry_delay(retry_error, 0, 1, 64)

12.0


_retry_action chooses wait, refresh, or stop without performing the action. Its second result is the delay for wait, otherwise None. The 12-second server delay is rejected when it exceeds max_wait or no attempts remain.

test_eq(_retry_action(retry_error, 0, 3, can_refresh=False), ('wait', 12))
test_eq(_retry_action(retry_error, 0, 3, can_refresh=False, max_wait=10), ('stop', None))
test_eq(_retry_action(retry_error, 2, 3, can_refresh=False), ('stop', None))
_retry_action(retry_error, 0, 3, can_refresh=False)

('wait', 12.0)


A 401 permits a credential refresh only when credentials are available and no refresh has already been attempted. Exhausting the request attempts takes precedence over refreshing.

unauthorized = APIError('Unauthorized', status_code=401)
test_eq(_retry_action(unauthorized, 0, 3, can_refresh=True), ('refresh', None))
test_eq(_retry_action(unauthorized, 1, 3, can_refresh=False), ('stop', None))
test_eq(_retry_action(unauthorized, 2, 3, can_refresh=True), ('stop', None))
_retry_action(unauthorized, 0, 3, can_refresh=True)

('refresh', None)




source

GWSTransport
def GWSTransport(
    *args, gcls:NoneType=None, creds:NoneType=None, **kwargs
):
Thin async transport over httpx2. By default each request gets a fresh client, so nothing is tied to an event loop; pass client= to use a persistent client that you manage (and close via aclose).


GWSTransport reads the current credential token when constructing request headers. Updating the credentials changes the next request’s authorization header. These example tokens are not sent to Google.

example_creds = Credentials('example-token')
authed_transport = GWSTransport(creds=example_creds)
test_eq(authed_transport._request_headers()['Authorization'], 'Bearer example-token')
example_creds.token = 'replacement-token'
auth_header = authed_transport._request_headers()['Authorization']
test_eq(auth_header, 'Bearer replacement-token')
auth_header

'Bearer replacement-token'




source

GWSTransport.request
async def request(
    *args, raw:bool=False, n_retries:int=5, # Maximum attempts, including the initial request
    base:float=1.0, # Initial exponential backoff and jitter range, in seconds
    max_backoff:float=64.0, # Maximum exponential component, in seconds
    max_wait:float=300.0, # Maximum individual retry wait, in seconds
    headers:NoneType=None, params:NoneType=None, json:NoneType=None, data:NoneType=None, files:NoneType=None,
    content:NoneType=None
):
Execute a request and decode JSON/text/binary response.


GWSTransport.request performs the selected retry action and preserves the original exception when retries stop. Successful JSON responses become GWSObject values. This request finds Drive in Google’s public API directory without credentials.

directory = await GWSTransport().request('GET', 'https://discovery.googleapis.com/discovery/v1/apis')
drive_entry = first(o for o in directory['items'] if o.name == 'drive' and o.preferred)
test_eq(drive_entry.version, 'v3')
test_is(type(drive_entry), GWSObject)
drive_entry.name, drive_entry.version

('drive', 'v3')

title: core
text:
HTTP batching


source

response_from_bytes
def response_from_bytes(
    data, request
):
Parse one complete HTTP response for request; raise h11.RemoteProtocolError for invalid framing




source

request_bytes
def request_bytes(
    request
):
Serialize a buffered httpx2.Request as HTTP/1.1


request_bytes writes an HTTP/1.1 message from an httpx2.Request. response_from_bytes reads one complete response for that request. HTTP framing is handled by h11. The response retains its headers and decoded body.

request = httpx2.Request('GET', 'https://api.example/things/one')
wire = b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\none\r\ntwo'
response = response_from_bytes(wire, request)
test_eq(response.content, b'one\r\ntwo')
response.status_code, response.content

(200, b'one\r\ntwo')




source

GWSOpFunc
def GWSOpFunc(
    op_spec, client, base_url, form_encoder:NoneType=None, defaults:NoneType=None
):


Each batch call supplies the same arguments as an individual GWSOpFunc operation. These two calls become separate HTTP requests inside one MIME body.

batch_spec = OpSpec(group='things', name='get', path='things/{id}', verb='GET', route_params=['id'])
batch_op = GWSOpFunc(batch_spec, GWSTransport(), 'https://api.example/', noop)
batch_content,batch_requests = batch_op._batch_content([dict(id='one'), dict(id='two')], 'requests')
test_eq([r.url.path for r in batch_requests], ['/things/one', '/things/two'])
PrettyString(batch_content.decode())

--requests
Content-Type: application/http
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-ID: <0>

GET /things/one HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example


--requests
Content-Type: application/http
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-ID: <1>

GET /things/two HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example


--requests--


Multipart responses are decoded back into ordered objects or structured APIError values before retry handling.
A multipart response can contain both a resource and an error. This example uses two GET calls and a response body written in the batch wire format.

batch_body = rb"""--response
Content-Type: application/http

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"one"}
--response
Content-Type: application/http

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"Quota exceeded","errors":[{"reason":"userRateLimitExceeded"}]}}
--response--
"""
batch_response = httpx2.Response(200, headers={'Content-Type':'multipart/mixed; boundary=response'}, content=batch_body)

Decoded results retain call order. The successful resource remains available while retry handling considers the rate-limit error.

batch_results = batch_op._batch_results(batch_response, batch_requests)
test_eq(batch_results[0].id, 'one')
test_eq((batch_results[1].status_code, batch_results[1].retryable), (403, True))
batch_results[0], batch_results[1].status_code

(GWSObject(id='one'), 403)


Each batch chunk uses _retry_action to decide which failed parts to retry. Successful results stay in place. A chunk refreshes credentials at most once after a 401 and waits for the longest delay required by its remaining parts. Retry options apply to both the batch HTTP request and its failed parts.


source

GWSOpFunc.batch
async def batch(
    calls, # Dictionaries of operation arguments, in result order
    chunk:int=50, # Calls per batch request, at most 100
    return_exceptions:bool=False, # Return per-call APIError values instead of raising
    n_retries:int=5, # Maximum attempts for each batch request and failed part
    base:float=1.0, # Initial exponential backoff and jitter range, in seconds
    max_backoff:float=64.0, # Maximum exponential component, in seconds
    max_wait:float=300.0, # Maximum individual retry wait, in seconds
):
Run dictionaries of arguments for this operation through Google’s discovery-advertised HTTP batch endpoint, retrying only the failed parts


batch preserves input order, retries only failed parts, and optionally returns structured per-call errors.

title: core
text:
Discovery clients
GWSApi builds a dynamic client from a Google discovery document and shares its authenticated transport across generated operations.


source

GWSApi
def GWSApi(
    service:NoneType=None, # Discovery API name, such as 'gmail', 'calendar', 'drive', 'docs', or 'sheets'
    version:NoneType=None, # API version, defaulting to the service's preferred version
    token:NoneType=None, # OAuth access token, as an alternative to `creds`
    creds:NoneType=None, # google-auth credentials, such as from `oauth_creds` or `svc_acct_creds`
    api_key:NoneType=None, # API key, defaulting to `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GWS_API_KEY` when there are no `creds` or `token`
    headers:NoneType=None, # Extra request headers
    timeout:float=60.0, # Request timeout in seconds
    doc:NoneType=None, # Discovery document to use, instead of fetching it
):
Client for one Google API, built from its discovery document, with resources as attribute groups such as gmail.users.messages




source

GWSApi.from_discovery_url
async def from_discovery_url(
    url, service:NoneType=None, version:NoneType=None, token:NoneType=None, creds:NoneType=None,
    api_key:NoneType=None, headers:NoneType=None, quota_project:NoneType=None, timeout:float=60.0
):
Create a client from a discovery document fetched from url


Some Google APIs publish a discovery document outside the central index or require authentication just to fetch it. from_discovery_url loads these services directly while reusing the same credentials, API key, quota project, headers, and transport configuration for subsequent operations.

drive_url = 'https://www.googleapis.com/discovery/v1/apis/drive/v3/rest'
drive_from_url = await GWSApi.from_discovery_url(drive_url)
test_eq((drive_from_url.service, drive_from_url.version), ('drive', 'v3'))
test_eq(drive_from_url.files.list.verb, 'GET')
list(drive_from_url.groups)

['revisions',
 'teamdrives',
 'changes',
 'replies',
 'accessproposals',
 'channels',
 'drives',
 'operations',
 'about',
 'apps',
 'files',
 'permissions',

Google list operations expose pages, which forwards each nextPageToken until the response has no next page.

batch can fetch the messages listed on the two pages above in one request. Results follow the order of calls. With return_exceptions=True, a failed call returns an APIError alongside successful messages instead of raising.

calls = [dict(user_id='me', id=p.messages[0].id, format='metadata') for p in (page1, page2)]
messages = await gmail.users.messages.get.batch(calls, return_exceptions=True)
test_eq(len(messages), len(calls))

title: admin
text: WorkspaceAdmin keeps the Admin Directory and Enterprise License Manager clients together. User creation, licensing, suspension, and deletion remain separate operations, so callers choose the lifecycle they need.

title: admin
text:
Users
Construct the administrator from credentials that include admin.directory.user and apps.licensing. create_user mirrors Google’s required identity fields while keeping the password and organizational policy explicit.

WorkspaceAdmin
def WorkspaceAdmin(
    creds
):
High-level Workspace user and license administration. creds need the admin.directory.user and apps.licensing scopes.

title: admin
text:
Licences and lifecycle
Licensing is deliberately independent from creation because a domain can auto-assign a licence by organizational unit. assign_license and remove_license use explicit product and SKU IDs; suspension and deletion only change the Directory user.

A complete provisioning sequence stays explicit:
scopes = ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user',
          'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/apps.licensing']
creds = await oauth_creds(account='admin@example.com', scopes=scopes)
admin = WorkspaceAdmin(creds)
user = await admin.create_user('new@example.com', 'New', 'User', password,
                               org_unit_path='/Internal')
await admin.assign_license(user.primaryEmail, 'workspace-sku-id')
If the organizational unit auto-licenses new users, inspect the assignment first and omit the final call.
